deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. Ff. 12r–12v (and following) tabulate primes p ≡ 3 (mod 8): 107, 131, 139, 163, 179, 211, 227, 251, 283, 307, 331, ... For each prime Gauss records three things.

(i) Header 'o.N'. N is the number of properly primitive classes of binary forms ax²+2bxy+cy² of determinant b²−ac = −p. For p ≡ 3 (mod 8), N = 3·h(−p):
- 163: 3
- 107, 139, 211, 283, 307, 331: 9
- 131, 179, 227: 15
- 251: 21
The group is cyclic in every listed case. Gauss labels the classes by exponents 0, 1, ..., N−1 with respect to a chosen generator. He writes each class together with its inverse ('Cl. 5.10' means classes g^5 and g^10 = g^−5).

(ii) 'Disc.' ('Discerptio', decomposition). These are the decompositions of p into three odd squares, p = a²+b²+c².

(iii) 'c:' (presumably 'continet'). This lists small numbers m, mostly primes, properly represented by the class. On this page it adds 'm(β, m−β)': the two roots of β² ≡ −p (mod m). These are the middle coefficients of the forms (m, ±β, (β²+p)/m).

TOP OF PAGE. 'Cl.2.7, Cl.4.5' finishes p = 211 (o.9), decomposition 121+81+9 from f.12r. No data is filled in.

p = 227, o.15 (h(−227) = 5). The 15 classes are 0..14.
- 227 = 225+1+1 ↔ classes {0, 5, 10}. Class 0 contains 1; classes 5/10 contain 4, via the form (4, 1, 57).
- 227 = 169+49+9 ↔ {1,14}, {4,11}, {6,9}.
- 227 = 121+81+25 ↔ {2,13}, {3,12}, {7,8}.
The numbers m are left blank. Counting: 3 + 6 + 6 = 15 classes. In representations, 24 + 48 + 48 = 120 = r₃(227) = 24·h(−227).

p = 251, o.21 (h(−251) = 7). Classes 0..20.
- 121+121+9 ↔ {0}: 1, and {7,14}: 4(3,1).
- [121+81+49, written '121+81+25'] ↔ {1,20}: 31(20,11), 73(25,48); {6,15}: 3(1,2); {8,13}: 23(18,5).
- 169+81+1 ↔ {2,19}: 17(2,15); {5,16}: 7(6,1), 41(35,6); {9,12}: 103(77,26).
- 225+25+1 ↔ {3,18}: 13(10,3); {4,17}: 5(2,3); {10,11}: 67(34,33).

My reconstruction of the classes, using the 21 reduced forms of determinant −251:
- class ±1 = (12, ∓1, 21)
- ±2 = (15, ∓2, 17)
- ±3 = (13, ±3, 20)
- ±4 = (5, ±2, 51)
- ±5 = (7, ∓1, 36)
- ±6 = (3, ±1, 84)
- ±7 = (4, ±1, 63)
- ±8 = (12, ±5, 23)
- ±9 = (9, ±1, 28)
- ±10 = (15, ±7, 20)
- 0 = (1, 0, 251)

The order inside each parenthesis is oriented: the first root always lands in the class named first.
- 31 with β = 20 gives (31, 20, 21) ~ (12, −1, 21); 73 with β = 25 gives (73, 25, 12) ~ (12, −1, 21).
- 7 with β = 6 gives (7, 6, 41) ~ (7, −1, 36); 41 with β = 35 gives (41, 35, 36) ~ (7, −1, 36).

I checked the labelling by composition:
- g = (12, −1, 21) squared is (15, −2, 17), the first form of class 2.
- (3, 1, 84) composed with (7, −1, 36) is (15, −7, 20), which is class 11 = inverse of the first form of class 10.
All products of the listed m are compatible.

STRUCTURE GAUSS IS DISPLAYING (implicit; my formulation). The decomposition with two equal squares corresponds to the subgroup of order 3: {0, N/3, 2N/3}. Each decomposition into distinct squares corresponds to a coset {k, k+N/3, k+2N/3} together with its inverse coset.
- 251: {1, 8, 15} ∪ {20, 13, 6}; {2, 9, 16} ∪ inverses; {3, 10, 17} ∪ inverses.
- 227: {1, 6, 11} ∪ {14, 9, 4}; {2, 7, 12} ∪ {13, 8, 3}.
So decompositions correspond to classes of Cl(−p) modulo inversion. The order-3 subgroup is the kernel of Cl(−4p) → Cl(−p) and is generated by the form (4, 1, (p+1)/4).

p = 283, 307, 331 (o.9, h = 3). Subgroup {0, 3, 6}; the remaining classes {1,8}, {2,7}, {4,5}.
- 283: 121+81+81 ↔ 0, 3.6; 225+49+9 ↔ 1.8, 2.7, 4.5.
- 307: 289+9+9 ↔ 0, 3.6; 225+81+1 ↔ 1.8, 2.7, 4.5.
- 331: 169+81+81 ↔ 0, 3.6. The remaining decomposition, 225+81+25, presumably continues on the next page.
errors: p = 251: the decomposition written '121+81+25' is wrong; 121+81+25 = 227. The correct decomposition is 121+81+49 = 251, the only remaining one. It is a slip, probably copied from the 227 block directly above. The attached classes and represented numbers (31, 73, 3, 23) are correct for 251.

No other arithmetic errors found. Every root β with β² ≡ −p (mod m) checks: 31, 73, 3, 23, 17, 7, 41, 103, 13, 5, 67, and 4 (mod 4). The class labels are consistent with a cyclic group of order 21 generated by (12, −1, 21).
The class entries for 227, 283, 307, 331 and the end of 211 are left incomplete. These are omissions, not errors.

results.what: For p ≡ 3 mod 8, the number of properly primitive classes of determinant −p equals 3h(−p) (15, 21, 9, ...). The class group is cyclic here, and its classes are indexed by exponents of a generator.
results.modern_name: Class group Cl(−4p), with h(−4p) = 3h(−p) for p ≡ 3 mod 8; cyclic structure

results.what: Representation counts: r₃(p) = 24h(−p); decompositions of p into three squares are matched to classes of determinant −p.
results.modern_name: Gauss's three-squares theorem relating r₃(n) to class numbers

results.what: Explicit matching: the two-equal-squares decomposition ↔ the order-3 subgroup {0, N/3, 2N/3}, generated by the class of (4, 1, (p+1)/4). Each other decomposition ↔ a coset of this subgroup together with its inverse coset. Equivalently, decompositions ↔ classes of Cl(−p) modulo inversion.
results.modern_name: Class-group (torsor) action on representations by x²+y²+z²; kernel of Cl(−4p) → Cl(−p)
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Gauss art. 292; explicit group-action formulations by Venkov (1929/31), later Shemanske, Gross and others

results.what: Tabulating the roots β of β² ≡ −p (mod m) for each represented m, in an oriented order, to identify the class of (m, β, (β²+p)/m).
results.modern_name: Locating ideal classes via prime forms / roots of the discriminant mod m

deep.surprise_reason: The class-number and three-squares counts are published in the Disquisitiones. What this page adds is a working table with an oriented cyclic indexing of the class group. It systematically pairs each three-square decomposition with a specific coset of the order-3 subgroup modulo inversion. That anticipates the group-action viewpoint on sums of three squares usually made explicit only in the 20th century. Still, it is a natural consequence of Gauss's own art. 292 theory, so it is a notable unpublished detail rather than a new theorem.

transcription_corrections: The headers '0.15', '0.21', '0.9' are 'o.15', 'o.21', 'o.9' (letter o, as on the previous page). They mean the number of classes, 3h(−p).
In the 251 block the line read 'Disc. 121+81+25[?].c' really does show 25 in the image. It is Gauss's slip for 121+81+49.
'C. 8.13.c: 23[?](18,5[?])' should read '23(18,5)' without query marks; 18 and 5 are the roots of β² ≡ −251 (mod 23).
